c.tagline: Russia's subtropical Black Sea resort, from palm-lined beaches to Olympic ski slopes.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked through the Yandex Go app, which is cheap and reliable; street taxis are unmetered, so agree a price first. Note that foreign bank cards do not work in Russia - carry cash or a local card.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified emergency number (you can also dial 102 for police, 103 for ambulance, 101 for fire).

avoid.reason: Avoid crossing into nearby Abkhazia just south of Adler — a disputed territory with border restrictions and consular no-go status.
Watch for overcharging taxis, inflated beach-vendor and photo-with-animal scams along the seafront promenade in high summer.

hood_desc: The lively heart of the resort, with the seafront promenade, Riviera Park, the Winter Theatre, the Sochi Arboretum (Dendrarium), and the main shopping and dining; the walkable base for most first-time visitors.

The southern district by the airport and railway hub, home to the 2014 Olympic Park, Sochi Park theme park, the Imeretinskaya beachfront, and the newest resort hotels; great tourist infrastructure and family beaches.

The mountain resort town about 40 km inland, base for the Rosa Khutor, Gazprom, and Gorky Gorod ski areas that hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics; alpine hotels and cable cars, with skiing in winter and hiking in summer.
A quieter green district between central Sochi and Adler, known for its pebble beaches, subtropical parks, and the Tisosamshitovaya (yew-boxwood) grove; relaxed and residential.
A historic spa quarter famous for its sulfur-rich balneological baths, set in wooded hills just south of the center; a calm, wellness-focused retreat.
lodging: Park Inn by Radisson Rosa Khutor

water.note: Locals often boil tap water; visitors are safest with bottled.

transit.pay: City bus fares are paid on board by cash or (local) contactless card, roughly 40 rubles a ride; there is no separate smartcard. The Lastochka commuter trains run along the coast between central Sochi, Khosta, Adler, the airport, and up to Krasnaya Polyana, with tickets bought at stations or the RZD app.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6am to 11pm; Lastochka coastal trains run frequently through the day, with ride-hailing (Yandex Go) filling the late-night gap.
transit.note: Sochi has no metro or tram. The backbone is an extensive city bus network plus the Lastochka electric coastal trains that link the strung-out districts of Greater Sochi and climb to the mountain resorts at Krasnaya Polyana.

transit.m: Aeroexpress / Lastochka train to central Sochi, ~50 min
City bus to Adler and central Sochi, ~60 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; leaving around 10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated.

landmarks: Sochi Arboretum (Dendrarium)
A lush hillside botanical park of subtropical flora from around the world, crossed by a cable car with sweeping Black Sea views.
Sochi Olympic Park
The 2014 Winter Games legacy site in Adler, where Fisht Stadium, the Bolshoy Ice Dome and a singing fountain surround the Olympic flame plaza.
Rosa Khutor (Krasnaya Polyana)
Russia's premier alpine resort in the Caucasus above Sochi, with year-round cable cars, an Olympic ski area and a chalet-lined river promenade.
Sochi Marine Terminal (Morskoy Vokzal)
An elegant Stalin-era seaport building crowned by a slender spired tower, the emblematic symbol of the Soviet Riviera.
Riviera Park
Sochi's beloved 1898 amusement park of shaded promenades, rides, a famous Friendship Alley of celebrity-planted magnolias and seaside fun.
Mount Akhun Tower
A romanesque stone observation tower atop 663-metre Mount Akhun, offering the classic panorama from snowy Caucasus peaks to the Black Sea coast.
Agura Waterfalls
A chain of waterfalls and jade pools in a wooded gorge beneath the Eagle Rocks, one of Sochi's most popular short hikes.
Stalin's Dacha (Green Grove)
The dictator's camouflage-green summer villa preserved with original furnishings, wax figure and billiard room in a secluded coastal park.
Skypark AJ Hackett Sochi
A 439-metre pedestrian suspension bridge strung across the Akhshtyr Gorge, with bungee jumps and giant swings above the Mzymta River.
Winter Theatre
A stately 1938 neoclassical theatre ringed by 88 Corinthian columns, the grande dame of Sochi's cultural life and festival stage.

train.note: No regular international passenger trains operate from Sochi - the seasonal service toward Sukhum in Abkhazia is the only cross-border option and its status varies. Sochi is the end of a scenic coastal main line: Lastochka electric trains shuttle between central Sochi, Khosta, Adler, the airport and Krasnaya Polyana, while long-distance RZD services including overnight trains run to Krasnodar, Rostov-on-Don, Moscow and St Petersburg. Foreign cards often fail on the RZD site.

bus.note: No scheduled international coaches. Intercity and long-distance coaches from Sochi's bus station serve Krasnodar, Rostov-on-Don and other cities across southern Russia and the North Caucasus; marshrutka minibuses run the length of the coastal strip and up to Krasnaya Polyana. Tickets are sold at the terminal.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Sochi. The Black Sea routes to Trabzon in Turkey and to Georgia have not operated reliably for years and should not be counted on. The seaport handles cruise calls and coastal excursion boats along the Sochi shoreline in summer.

half.name: Vorontsov Caves
half.blurb: Limestone cave system in forested hills above Khosta, with chambers open for guided walking tours.

full.name: New Athos
full.blurb: Former Soviet resort town across the border with a 19th-century monastery and a large karst cave.

full.name: Lake Ritsa
full.blurb: Mountain lake in the Caucasus surrounded by forested peaks, reached by a winding road from the coast.
